name: rust-engine-frontier
title: Rust-engine frontier: where a Rust path pays off (dispatch) and where it does not (ODE integration)
question:
The Rust engines (viva-core, viva-hybrid) are often assumed to be a drop-in
speedup. Where on the performance frontier do they actually sit relative to the
tellurium+vivarium baseline this workspace benchmarks — and can viva-core even
run our decomposed composites today?
hypothesis:
A Rust path accelerates bigraph *dispatch* (scheduling process updates), not ODE
*integration*. viva-core runs only processes registered in its native Rust
registry, so our Python/tellurium/COPASI composites cannot run there without a
Rust-side port; and viva-hybrid, the strongest Rust SSA attempt, is a rigorous
negative result (no regime both >=5x faster and faithful to exact SSA).
objective:
Attempt, best-effort, to run the one portable arm (the native glycolysis
composite) through viva-core's engine; record either the measured ODE speedup or
the honest "requires a Rust-side process port" finding; and situate it against
viva-core's cited ~1.27x scalar-dispatch benchmark and viva-hybrid's ~2x negative
result. Grade the honest characterization, not a Rust win.
description:
Phase 6 of the clarity + capabilities program (G6). The spike
(viva_sbml_decomposition.harness.rust_frontier) feeds the native composite
document to viva_core.run(). The measured outcome on this machine: viva-core
imports and runs, but REJECTS the native composite —
`address "local:NativeGlycolysisProcess" is not module.Class` — because the
process is not in viva-core's native Rust registry. So the engine cannot run our
composites without a Rust-side port, which is itself the honest frontier finding;
no ODE speedup is claimed.

The committed machine-tagged baseline (visualizations/rust_frontier.json) records
this, plus the attributed context — viva-core accelerates dispatch (~1.27x scalar,
cited from its own benchmark, regresses on array-heavy state) and viva-hybrid's
rigorous ~2x-over-numba negative result. The grade is code-authoritative and reads
only that committed JSON (no Rust toolchain in CI): it PASSES on an honest
characterization and FAILS any result that would assert a >=5x ODE-acceleration win
the engine did not earn. This is explicitly NOT a Rust ODE kernel or a
native-process registration — it frames where a Rust path would and would not pay
off for this workspace.

expected_behavior.name: rust-frontier-characterized-honestly
expected_behavior.observable: the committed viva-core spike result (requires_port / ode_speedup) and its dispatch-vs-ODE characterization
expected_behavior.condition: the result asserts no unearned Rust ODE-acceleration win — either the composite requires a Rust-side port, or no ODE speedup was measured, or any measured ODE speedup is modest (< 5x) — and the dispatch-vs-ODE distinction is documented
expected_behavior.rationale: the point of the phase is an honest frontier, not a manufactured speedup; a result claiming a large ODE win viva-core did not earn would defeat it.
